Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor was gained by entering through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and 
the first fifteen rotating and stationary stages were inspected.  Access to stages 15, 16, and 17 was gained 
though the opened right side CDC ports.

4. New variables, landing points, screen changes, logic review: 
 
Created variables (DWATT3 and DVAR1) and landing points as per customer request, to accommodate newly added 
MWATT and MVAR transmitters. 
 
Fixed screen issue on GEN / EXCITER pages (Block 1 & 2), where switching between the gas turbines would black out 
the data fields. The script commanding the change was found missing the necessary parameters to address the 
correct exciters for each GT. 
 
Customer concern – Online DC lube oil pump test is tripping gas turbine. 
o Discussed trip circumstances with customer and identified root cause. 
No logic change is necessary, customer to update their internal procedure. 
 
Updated hydraulic oil filter differential pressure transmitter range (96HF1 / 2 from max 150 psi to 100 psi) on GT1/GT2 
as per customer request 
 
5. Pre-start calibrations and checks 
 
Calibrated IGV on G3 & G4 – measurements were taken by the Mech. TFA, witnessed by on site performance engineer. 
 
Stroked all 4 compressor bleed valves on G3 & G4 
 
Stroked all gas valves (SRV, PM1, PM2, PM3, Quat, AFS) on G3 & G4 
 
Online water wash spray pattern test and leak checks on G3 & G4 
 
Stroked IBH valves on G3 & G4 
 
Verified correct installation of wheel space thermocouples on G3 and G4 
 
6. ST2 CV2 valve troubleshooting: 
 
Following calibration of the CV2 valve was found to be opening sluggish and unable to maintain position while 
moving to a lower opening percentage. 
 
Control side was found functioning as expected. 
 
Both filters were opened, no debris was found in them. 
 
Customer replaced the servo and operation returned to normal.

bellmouth casing were made with OSS team on site, and new nozzles were installed. As part

WW nozzle manifold. The regulator was provisionally set to 80psig, to be revised when the 
new water wash skid is installed Tubing towards a new transducer 96WW was provided from 
the manifold to the turbine compartment penetration, but not completed up to the JB. New 
nozzles were tested at 80 psig prior to inlet closeout.

A borescope inspection was performed on the compressor section of the unit. An 
Engineering case was opened to disposition the compressor based on the inspection report. 
The following recommendation was provided :
IGV bushings have migrated. They should be pushed back and staked.
Apart from that the observations noted in the BI report the compressor looks fine.
Recommend to perform a good off line water wash before returning the unit to service.
Also site should follow up proper procedures when shutting down/starting up to avoid rubs.

This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the generator described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, greasing, dusting, oil contamination, corona, hot spots, arcing, 
rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other

Color images depicting the condition of the generator were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the generator was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography.

Customer concern: Over 40 network related alarms 
 
4108 network specification and drawings, network switch settings were reviewed.  
Found thin clients and servers configured different than 4108, corrected settings and that eliminated most of the 
network alarms. 
 
Cooling fan in SW5-1 was found inoperable. Replacements was ordered (no OEM available) from a 3rd party supplier. 
 
Replaced cooling fan in SW5-1 and SW5-2 (SW5-2 was found having mechanical noise) 
 
HS2 server reported a failed internal microSD card in the mirror. 
New card was purchased, all virtual machines shut down on HS2. 
Server was put in maintenance mode and shut down. New microSD card was installed, ESXi mirror rebuilt. 
After reboot, server was removed from maintenance mode and all VMs started up. Functionality was verified and 
server returned to normal operation. 
 
2. Water Wash upgrade on G3 & G4: 
 
Due to logistical challenges, water wash skid did not arrive on time to complete the upgrade. 
 
Requisition engineering provided software was not installed – this step needed to be skipped to maintain 
functionality of the old WW skid. 
 
Software was reviewed by Req. Engr., removed all WW related modifications, applying only the safety changes. 
 
Old GT SW was replaced with this updated one. 
 
3. Control constant upgrades on G3 / G4 : 
 
As part of AFS uprate, control constants had to be updated on both turbines. 
 
Received updated A010 (DWG: 312T0591 REV -), discussed contents with requisition and performance engineering and 
carried out changes as requested. Both live values and initial values were updated and downloaded. 
 
Deviations from A010 were requested by performance engineering based on their calculations: 
o Lowered IGV max angle (CSKGVMX from 88 to 84 degrees) 
o Lowered KCA_GFTF_MX array numbers 
o 1st STG Nozzle constants (KCA_S1NA) were updated based on cold area calculations from the nozzle reports. 
o 1st STG Nozzle fired hours (KTFT_S1NA) were updated according to the current counters. 
 
Customer lost G1 fired hours following a controller reboot earlier. Password was requested and totalizer updated with 
correct numbers, based on site records.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor was gained by entering through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and 
the first fifteen rotating and stationary stages were inspected.  Access to stages 15, 16, and 17 was gained 
though the opened right side CDC ports.

Borescope Inspection
When unit next has it's End-Shields removed, some cleaning of the greasing 
should be performed.      This should be followed by the application of Red-
Eye 2-Part Resin (MSD-A50A244A0G0052) with Flooding 2-Part Resin (MSD-

This will assist in preventing further fretting/movement of the end-winding 
hardware and by default reduce greasing also.
Short Turn Test
Perhaps an RSO could be carried out during the next outage to give a clearer 
picture on condition of the end-winding turns.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the generator described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, greasing, dusting, oil contamination, corona, hot spots, arcing, 
rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other 
abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the generator were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the generator was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access for the borescope was made through the manhole covers on TE and CE End-Shields.

stop seating. On the final closeout, Liner #5 and liner #9 were found to have minor TBC

TIL 2441 IMPLEMENTATION 
causing current to arc across the gap until the gap becomes too large for the arc to be sustained. 
This action is like slowly opening a knife switch in an inductive circuit. The arcing can go on for 
hours, even days, before the field circuit opens, ending the flashover event. 
Flashover events have been part of the power industry since the first use of slip rings (collector 
rings). Most flashover events may be avoided with proper preventative maintenance as 
described in the operations and maintenance manuals. 
In the static exciter (EX2100*/EX2100e*) software, the parameter DC_FaultOC (DC Fault trip 
amps) is the DC current level (amps) that will cause instantaneous over-current to become active 
and trip the exciter. This value is typically kept at less than five times the shunt rating. This value 
(<5 x ShuntAmps) was originally configured by considering the equipment's withstanding. 
capability during such over-current events. The hazard of exposure to the arc flash energy can be 
limited by reducing the field over-current trip settings, which reduces and limits the maximum 
field current that flows during an arcing event and thus reduces the arc flash energy. 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
In order to reduce the arc flash energy during some collector flashover event conditions, it is 
recommended for units subject to this TIL to reduce the DC Fault trip amps to three times the 
shunt rating in the exciter software followed by download of software to all controllers (M1, M2, 
and C) and reboot. 
1-The ShuntAmps is 2000Adc and the DC fault trip amps (DC_FaultOC) is 9000Adc, which is 4.5 
times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for 
(E1, E2, E3, &E4). from 9000Adc to 6000Adc  
2-The ShuntAmps is 2500Adc and the DC fault trip amps (DC_FaultOC) is 11250Adc, which is 4.5 
times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for  
modify DC_FaultOC for (X1 &X2) from 11250Adc to 7500Adc.   
 
Lastly, after completing the above recommendations it is also advised to recalculate the arc-flash 
potential requirements to ensure that the maintenance personnel have the right level of PPE 
required to perform online maintenance of the collector. GEK116362 section II Safety can be 
referred for further details. 
This TIL is considered complete when the parameter DC_FaultOC is updated, and software is 
downloaded to the controllers followed by a reboot.

M
Inspection Type: Visual
Part Condition: Good
Part Description: 
During this outage all of the flexible metal hoses (FMH) were removed from service and 
staged for inspection. The FMHs were internally borescoped and the outer skin visually 
inspected for flex armor integrity as per TIL 1585. Note that all flex-hoses were installed with 
new seals while keeping to the recommendations outlined in Technical Information Letters 
TIL 1237-1 Possible Flexible Hose Installation Errors and GT-1101 Remove Combustion End 
Cover Piping. Additionally, each flex hose was blown out with compressed air just prior to 
installation.
As part of AGP Tech upgrade, new orifices were installed in the Air Extraction lines as per 
FMI.
Recommendation Description: 
GE recommends periodic inspections of the cooling water, water wash, and water injection 
turbine compartment piping systems in order to maintain proper performance. These 
inspections should be conducted at every maintenance outage. During these inspections, 
perform the following:
• Verify piping and tubing is properly supported and is not rubbing or abrading in any way.
• Check for any damage, wear, loose fittings, interference, fretting, or anything else that may 
lead to leaks or system malfunctions.
• When inspecting flame scanner cooling coils, ensure that the clamp is not in contact with 
the cooling tubes. Verify that the flame detector cooling coils are tight, with no relative 
motion between the clamp and cooling coils.

Part Description: 
AFS Manifolds and inner tubing assemblies were all disassembled and inspected. The 
tubing assemblies were replaced with a new set. Prior to installation new and old tubing 
were laid side by side, inspected for any major deviations on tube bends, dampener 
assemblies and for any other defects. New bolts and locktabs were used to affix the tubing 
assemblies to the new TP's. While installing the tubing assembly on Can#5, one of the bolts 
were galled into the nozzle bolthole. This was drilled out and a new helicoil and bolt were 
installed. Old retainer brackets were installed with some old hardware after obtaining 
engineering clearance and performing a red-dye penetrant test on relevant areas. New C-
seals were installed on the fuel posts. A site-made 2 1/4" crow's foot was used to torque the 
Fuel post nut. AFS manifold was reassembled with new 2" 300 gaskets.

TIL 2441 IMPLEMENTATION 
causing current to arc across the gap until the gap becomes too large for the arc to be sustained. 
This action is like slowly opening a knife switch in an inductive circuit. The arcing can go on for 
hours, even days, before the field circuit opens, ending the flashover event. 
Flashover events have been part of the power industry since the first use of slip rings (collector 
rings). Most flashover events may be avoided with proper preventative maintenance as 
described in the operations and maintenance manuals. 
In the static exciter (EX2100*/EX2100e*) software, the parameter DC_FaultOC (DC Fault trip 
amps) is the DC current level (amps) that will cause instantaneous over-current to become active 
and trip the exciter. This value is typically kept at less than five times the shunt rating. This value 
(<5 x ShuntAmps) was originally configured by considering the equipment's withstanding. 
capability during such over-current events. The hazard of exposure to the arc flash energy can be 
limited by reducing the field over-current trip settings, which reduces and limits the maximum 
field current that flows during an arcing event and thus reduces the arc flash energy. 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
In order to reduce the arc flash energy during some collector flashover event conditions, it is 
recommended for units subject to this TIL to reduce the DC Fault trip amps to three times the 
shunt rating in the exciter software followed by download of software to all controllers (M1, M2, 
and C) and reboot. 
1-The ShuntAmps is 2000Adc and the DC fault trip amps (DC_FaultOC) is 9000Adc, which is 4.5 
times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for 
(E1, E2, E3, &E4). from 9000Adc to 6000Adc  
2-The ShuntAmps is 2500Adc and the DC fault trip amps (DC_FaultOC) is 11250Adc, which is 4.5 
times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for  
modify DC_FaultOC for (X1 &X2) from 11250Adc to 7500Adc.   
 
Lastly, after completing the above recommendations it is also advised to recalculate the arc-flash 
potential requirements to ensure that the maintenance personnel have the right level of PPE 
required to perform online maintenance of the collector. GEK116362 section II Safety can be 
referred for further details. 
This TIL is considered complete when the parameter DC_FaultOC is updated, and software is 
downloaded to the controllers followed by a reboot.

were cleaned and oil stoned prior to reassembly. All threaded holes, including shroud pin 
holes, nozzle plug holes, and turbine borescope and clearanceometer plug holes were 
cleaned and tapped prior to reassembly.

Customer concern: Over 40 network related alarms 
 
4108 network specification and drawings, network switch settings were reviewed.  
Found thin clients and servers configured different than 4108, corrected settings and that eliminated most of the 
network alarms. 
 
Cooling fan in SW5-1 was found inoperable. Replacements was ordered (no OEM available) from a 3rd party supplier. 
 
Replaced cooling fan in SW5-1 and SW5-2 (SW5-2 was found having mechanical noise) 
 
HS2 server reported a failed internal microSD card in the mirror. 
New card was purchased, all virtual machines shut down on HS2. 
Server was put in maintenance mode and shut down. New microSD card was installed, ESXi mirror rebuilt. 
After reboot, server was removed from maintenance mode and all VMs started up. Functionality was verified and 
server returned to normal operation. 
 
2. Water Wash upgrade on G3 & G4: 
 
Due to logistical challenges, water wash skid did not arrive on time to complete the upgrade. 
 
Requisition engineering provided software was not installed – this step needed to be skipped to maintain 
functionality of the old WW skid. 
 
Software was reviewed by Req. Engr., removed all WW related modifications, applying only the safety changes. 
 
Old GT SW was replaced with this updated one. 
 
3. Control constant upgrades on G3 / G4 : 
 
As part of AFS uprate, control constants had to be updated on both turbines. 
 
Received updated A010 (DWG: 312T0591 REV -), discussed contents with requisition and performance engineering and 
carried out changes as requested. Both live values and initial values were updated and downloaded. 
 
Deviations from A010 were requested by performance engineering based on their calculations: 
o Lowered IGV max angle (CSKGVMX from 88 to 84 degrees) 
o Lowered KCA_GFTF_MX array numbers 
o 1st STG Nozzle constants (KCA_S1NA) were updated based on cold area calculations from the nozzle reports. 
o 1st STG Nozzle fired hours (KTFT_S1NA) were updated according to the current counters. 
 
Customer lost G1 fired hours following a controller reboot earlier. Password was requested and totalizer updated with 
correct numbers, based on site records.
